title: Family Law Amendment (Federal Family Violence Orders) Bill 2021
short_title: Family Law Amendment (Federal Family Violence Orders) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create federal family violence protection orders enforceable through criminal offences, allowing specified family law courts to issue them within existing proceedings.
Courts could restrict behaviour, contact and access to places, with breaches carrying up to two years' imprisonment, 120 penalty units, or both under federal law.
Orders could protect children, parents, certain carers and parties to a marriage, while state and territory police could enforce breaches through the national protection-order scheme.
changes: Protected people could not be charged with aiding or abetting a breach merely because their actions invited it.
Self-induced intoxication could not support claims of accidental conduct or mistaken belief about facts.
State and territory courts could suspend or revoke federal orders in specified circumstances when making or varying local orders.
Registrars conducting relevant family law or child support conferences would receive judicial protection and immunity.
summary.affected: Protected family members, people subject to orders, listed courts, registrars and state and territory police are affected.

speeches.speaker: Sussan Ley
speeches.brief: The government introduced the Family Law Amendment (Federal Family Violence Orders) Bill to establish federal family violence orders in family law courts, and acknowledged three Indigenous women—Jacinta Price, Cheron Long and Becky Long—visiting parliament to speak on women's safety in Indigenous communities.
